title: First sense: natural as belonging to nature's first institution
source_text: XIV. Primo enim naturale dicitur quod inest a prima institutione naturae. Et hac ratione dicit immortalitatem fuisse primo homini naturalem, mortem vero contra naturam, quoniam homo initio institutus est immortalis, id est, a moriendi necessitate liber.
pass_a_gloss: For first that is called natural which is present from the first institution of nature. And in this respect he says that immortality was natural to the first man, but death against nature, since man was instituted at the beginning immortal, that is, free from the necessity of dying.
pass_b_english: First, what is present from nature's first institution is called natural. In this sense he says that immortality was natural to the first man and death against nature, since man was created immortal at the beginning, that is, free from the necessity of dying.

lemmas.gloss: free from the necessity of dying

choices.why: Institutio here is God's first making of man; 'created' keeps the sense without the legal tone of 'instituted'.
